title: What Challenges Do Fashion Designers Face When Moving From Digital Garment Design to Production?
content:
Moving from a digital garment concept to physical production can introduce challenges that are not always obvious during the design stage.

Pattern accuracy, fabric behavior, grading, construction details, measurements, and sample fit can all affect how closely the finished garment matches the original design.

For designers working on new collections, I’m curious which part of this transition usually requires the most adjustment.

I’ve been reviewing apparel development workflows, including the process used by [Lydia Design Studio](https://www.lydiadesignstudio.com/)[,](https://www.lydiadesignstudio.com/) where design development moves through pattern making, sampling, grading, and production.

For those working with physical samples after creating digital garments, what tends to be the biggest challenge: fit, fabric selection, pattern adjustments, or construction?
content_description: Exploring the key challenges designers face when transitioning digital garment concepts into accurate, well-fitting physical samples through pattern making, fabric selection, grading, and construction.

title: GLB Export shows shiny black surfaces in model viewer
content:
Hi,

When I export a Clo3D model as a GLB and open it in a model viewer, it shows shiny black surfaces in some seemingly random places.

These are the export settings:

![80ffacb9688e4c7782a6101a586d965e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/5afb0d97643442d191b5ba45fe8c1796/images/80ffacb9688e4c7782a6101a586d965eimage.png)

And this is how it ends up looking in an online Model Viewer:

![c3a4cf7ce0d24289a2fc7b3fe2a0b086](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202609/5afb0d97643442d191b5ba45fe8c1796/images/c3a4cf7ce0d24289a2fc7b3fe2a0b086image.png)

Can anyone assist me in what I'm doing wrong? 

Thanks,

Stijn

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: HI. I cannot speak to all 3D model viewers. They each have their own quirks.But one idea I have is that you should always organize your UV maps in the grids. Usually all pattern pieces should be organized in just 1 UV square. You can use multiple as needed if you were using multiple fabrics, but the individual pattern pieces should not be in multiple squares at once. They need to be scaled to fit in the squares
content_description: A troubleshooting guide to resolve shiny black surface issues when exporting Clo3D models as GLB files for use in online 3D model viewers.

title: API - Importing .zpac changes the avatar.
content:
Hello. I am relatively new to CLO3D and am trying to automate a workflow using CLO3D's scripting API. First, I have an avatar loaded into the scene, however, when I use the import_api to import a garment from a .zpac file, it automatically adjusts the avatar.  
  
There is an ImportExportOption member named `bSizeAndPoseFromAvatar`, which I thought would fix it, but changing this value does nothing. Am I doing something wrong or is this a known issue?  
  
Alternatively, I could load the garment first, then the avatar, which avoids this issue. However, then I would like to know how i can automatically "move" the garment to the avatar such that it fits around the avatar.  
  
If anyone has any information, I would love to hear it. Thank you.
content_description: A forum page seeking advice on automating garment import in CLO3D without altering the avatar’s size or pose and methods to fit garments to avatars programmatically.
